newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Gle Eaux transport looks to Asia Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux transport looks to Asia Pacific.

text.p: The Asia Pacific transport subsidiary of French utility group Cie Generale des Eaux said on Wednesday agreements with Indonesia's State-owned railway Permuka marked the beginning of its moves into the region.

CGEA Transport Asia Pacific Pty Ltd managing director Claude Sauvage told Reuters the company, a wholly owned subsidiary of Generale's transport branch CGEA, was bidding or considering bids in Australia, the Philippines and New Zealand.

"It is a region which is moving very quickly, especially in transport, there are a lot of needs in Asia and a lot of public companies which are moving (towards privatisation) also in Australia," he said from the company's Adelaide base.
"So it is a priority for our group to be present and to develop our business here," he said.

Sauvage said CGEA had recently signed two agreements with Permuka for its Tangerang-Jakarta-Kota metropolitan service and for an original regional link servicing the tourism area around Jakarta-Bogor-Bandung.

Under the agreements, CGEA Asia Pacific would assess the links and provide technical assistance and, depending on their findings, would negotiate a possible agreement to jointly operate the lines, he said.
Sauvage said the deal, which included the French-contolled hotels, tourism and leisure group AAPC Ltd, confirmed CGEA's intention to expand into transport services in the Asia Pacific.

CGEA and Accor are part of a consortium, also involving international rail operators Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp and New Zealand's TranzRail, which has been shortlisted to bid for Australia's rail operator Australian National.
Sauvage said the company also would bid for the management of the train, bus and tram network in Melbourne, in the Australian state of Victoria, and for the New Zealand Yellow Bus Co.
